model: K45SS (Classic Series, 4.5 Qt Tilt-Head Stand Mixer)
tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own owner's manual documents the entire control surface as a single mechanical Speed Control lever moved between 10 marked detents, describes attachments (flat beater, wire whip, dough hook, and hub-driven accessories) purely mechanically, and contains no mention of an app, WiFi, Bluetooth, or programmable memory anywhere in 19 pages. Electrical section lists only voltage/frequency; a 250-watt universal motor per retailer listings.
the_unplug_test: You turn the speed lever to a number between 0 and 10 and the motor spins the attachment hub at that speed until you turn it back down. Tilting the head back locks it mechanically with a lever, not a sensor. Unplugging and replugging it returns it to exactly the same state, because there is no state to lose — no clock, no memory, no account, nothing that ever talks to KitchenAid.

repairability.notes: One of the most parts-supported small appliances sold: KitchenAid and third-party parts distributors stock beater shafts, motor brushes, gearing and the full attachment-hub ecosystem for this and adjacent tilt-head models spanning decades of production.

sources.supports: KitchenAid's own K45SSWH Owner's Manual (mirrored by a parts retailer): Tilt-Head Stand Mixer Features diagram labels a single 'Speed Control Knob'/lever; Speed Control Guide lists 10 numbered mechanical detents (Stir, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10) each tied to a mixing task; Electrical Requirements section lists only 120 V.A.C./60 Hz. No app, WiFi, Bluetooth, or digital-control feature appears anywhere in the 19-page manual.
Retailer listing title confirms the 250-watt motor rating and current sale of the K45SS model.

open_questions: The manual notes the wattage rating is printed on a tag under the mixer base rather than in the document itself; 250W is corroborated only by retailer listings, not the manual text directly.
notes: The baseline tilt-head KitchenAid mixer, essentially unchanged in control layout since the mid-20th century. KitchenAid does sell WiFi-connected mixers in other lines; this is the mechanical-lever entry point of the Classic/Artisan tilt-head family, distinguished by having no digital display of any kind.
